title: A headless runner's child inherits the session's SSH agent and push credentials, so code it edits and then runs can publish or push anywhere
goal: autopilot.py runner start runs its claude child with an environment that holds no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, SSH_AGENT_PID, GIT_ASKPASS, GITLAB_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN or other credential variable (autopilot.child_env), and gives the runner's worktree a failing pushurl for the public remote (git config remote.<public>.pushurl), so code an agent edits and then runs through an allowed command cannot push to the public home or a branch the integration credentials would allow; planted-failure tests read the child's environment and the worktree's config; the operator-only parts (a deploy key or token limited to code/* and main, server-side branch protection) are the operator's and outside this item; found by the SP-zihqagoi review

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import autopilot;sys.exit(0 if hasattr(autopilot,'child_env') else 1)

repro_reason: the leak shows only when a real runner's child pushes with the operator's SSH agent; the repro checks the scrubbed environment exists, the check plants a credential and reads the child's environment
